inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average for Q2 2026 (10-Q, 135.553M); basic shares on issue 134.680M at 2026-07-17 (10-Q cover). Held FLAT because SBC plus equity-award withholding taxes are expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $43.981M plus taxes paid on net-share settlement $14.887M (financing activities); Dover publishes no combined figure so the two lines are summed. H1 2026 run-rate is higher ($27.8M SBC + $31.9M withholding, Q1 vesting spike).
inputs.buyback_note: Actual financing outflow: FY2024 $500M, FY2025 $540.7M (incl. $500M ASR), H1 2026 $53.9M. Dover is a repurchaser, so the flat count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), beta ~1.05, ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~9.5%; debt ~11% of EV at ~4.6% pre-tax / 3.6% after-tax -> WACC ~8.8%, used as 8.75% in every scenario. Cyclicality is priced in the bear scenario's flows, not in a WACC premium (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost (~$65M/yr cash) sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside EBITDA; operating lease liabilities ($247M at FY2025) are excluded from net debt. Finance lease principal ($5.3M/yr) is immaterial. One treatment, lease cost in the flows; lease_cost_pct_path is zero because the charge is already in the margin.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing row: cyclical US industrial). Dover is a diversified manufacturer of equipment, components and consumables across five segments; no financial, property or holdco features, so the default operating-company engine applies. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry). ANCHORS: revenue base FY2025 $8,092.6M; FY2025 reported FCF (OCF continuing $1,338.0M - capex $220.3M) $1,117.7M = 13.8% of revenue; owner FCF $1,058.9M after SBC and equity-award taxes. Interest income ($73M FY2025) is NOT stripped from last_fcf because Dover is net debt, not net cash; the component build is unlevered from EBITDA, which excludes interest income and other non-operating income, and net debt is deducted once in the bridge. DATA ISSUE: the Metrics CSV TotalDebt column double-counts current maturities from FY2024 onward (e.g. Q2 2026 CSV 3,941.8 = LongTermDebt 3,260.0 + current portion 681.8, which is already inside LongTermDebt); this DCF uses XBRL LongTermDebt $3,260.0M (ties to stockanalysis D/E 0.42x on $7.7B equity). Cash here is cash+restricted cash $1,756.0M at 2026-06-30 (the CSV has no cash column after FY2020). MARGIN BASIS: ebitda_margin_path is GAAP EBITDA (operating earnings + all D&A) with SBC added back, i.e. restructuring (~1%/yr, recurring at Dover) and corporate expense stay IN as real costs; FY2025 = (1,752.9 + 44.0)/8,092.6 = 22.2%. Management's adjusted segment EBITDA margin (25.0% FY2025) is higher because it excludes corporate expense and restructuring. GROWTH: the path is organic plus FX only after FY2026; Dover also buys ~$600M/yr of bolt-ons (2024 $635M, 2025 $663M) which are outside capex and therefore outside owner FCF, so acquired growth is deliberately NOT projected (it would be growth without its purchase price). D&A glides from 4.6% to 2.6% (=capex) because ~half of today's D&A is acquired-intangible amortization that rolls off absent new deals; leaving it at 4.6% would perpetuate a tax shield the terminal business does not have. Working capital capture -15% of each revenue increase (manufacturer: receivables + inventory exceed payables). Cash tax 22% (FY2025 cash taxes $307.1M on pretax $1,374.3M = 22.3%; GAAP ETR 20.1%).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr cross-checked to FY2026 organic guidance (4-6%) and long-run organic record; equity CAGR rejected
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (17-20%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (1-4%) and EPS CAGRs. Book value was inflated by the FY2024 ~$1.9B after-tax gain on the ESG and De-Sta-Co divestitures (FY2024 EPS 19.58 is gain-driven); it is not an operating growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes): FY2020 885.6, FY2022 549.9, FY2023 1,126.0, FY2025 1,058.9. The 3yr FCF CAGR of 24% is off a FY2022 working-capital trough (supply-chain inventory build) and is not a run-rate; the 5yr 3.6% is the honest figure. The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR (3.64%) is slightly ABOVE reported (3.55%) because FY2020 withholding taxes were unusually high, so SBC is not outgrowing cash flow. Revenue history is portfolio-distorted: the FY2024 ESG/De-Sta-Co sales removed ~$1.2B of revenue, and the 3yr revenue CAGR of 1% understates underlying organic growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 = guidance midpoint (+6-8% reported incl. ~1.5pp acquisitions and ~1.5pp FX). Thereafter organic only (~3-4.5%): secular platforms (~25% of portfolio) growing high single digit offset by GDP-like legacy segments.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2026 22.8% implied by GAAP EPS guidance $8.94-9.14 (~+13% on 7% revenue) and H1 2026 21.7% pre-SBC with H2 seasonally stronger; +1.2pp over five years from mix and productivity, then flat at 24%.

scenario_narratives.base: Dover delivers FY2026 guidance (revenue +7%, GAAP EPS ~$9.04) on the record order book, then grows organically 3-4.5% a year: the secular platforms (CO2 refrigeration, cryogenic and data-centre thermal components, biopharma fluid handling, ~25% of the portfolio) grow high single digits while fueling, polymer processing and vehicle aftermarket track industrial production. The refrigeration facility consolidation that cost 1-1.5pp of Q2 growth is fixed within a year. GAAP EBITDA margin (pre-SBC) steps from 22.2% to 24% through mix and productivity, and owner-FCF margin settles near 15-16%, in line with the 14-16% FCF margin management guides. Bolt-on M&A continues but is treated as value-neutral and excluded.
scenario_narratives.bull: The secular platforms scale faster than the market expects: data-centre and LNG/hydrogen cryogenic demand, natural-refrigerant regulation in retail refrigeration and single-use biopharma connectors lift organic growth to 6-7% for several years, with 35-40% incrementals (Q2 2026 printed 38%) carrying the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 26%. Europe (organic -5% in Q2 2026) recovers and China stabilises. The market re-rates Dover from a diversified cyclical toward a growth-industrial multiple (18x terminal FCF).
scenario_narratives.bear: The industrial cycle turns in 2027: fueling and vehicle-wash capex, polymer processing and engineered products fall with customer capex, revenue drops ~3% and decremental margins take pre-SBC EBITDA to 20.5%. The refrigeration and cryogenic footprint consolidations (9 to 4 plants) keep slipping, tariffs and renminbi/euro translation dent reported results, and the secular platforms prove smaller and lumpier than the ~25% claim. Margin recovers only to 22%, growth settles at 2-2.5%, and the stock exits at a cyclical 13x FCF.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): Dover is a genuine cyclical, the order book is at a multi-year high which historically precedes normalisation, and Q2 2026 showed execution slippage in exactly the growth platforms the bull case relies on. Base 50%: guidance was raised and is anchored by backlog, so the central path has good near-term visibility. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it requires several independent things at once (secular platforms scaling, European recovery, sustained 35%+ incrementals and a multiple re-rating).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on an unlevered component build: SBC and equity-award withholding taxes expensed, share count held flat (Dover funds the flat count with buybacks), organic growth only (acquired growth excluded because acquisition spend sits outside owner FCF), acquired-intangible amortization allowed to roll off so the terminal year carries no phantom tax shield, and cyclicality priced in a recession bear case rather than in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Industrial-cycle timing: the bear path's 2027 revenue decline is a real possibility with bookings at a peak; a 2008-style drawdown (-29% revenue in FY2009) is worse than the bear case.
M&A: Dover spends ~$600M/yr on bolt-ons; if those earn above WACC the organic-only projection undervalues the capital-allocation engine, and if below, the base case is generous.

Terminal value is ~56% of base-case enterprise value (61% bull); each 1x of terminal FCF multiple is worth ~$6 per share in the base case, and the 16x cap binds in base (Gordon at 8.75%/2.5% would give ~16.4x).

Margin basis: the path is GAAP-EBITDA (restructuring and corporate cost included). Reading management's 25% adjusted segment EBITDA margin into the model instead would overstate value by roughly $25-30/share.
Secular-platform execution (refrigeration and cryogenic plant consolidations) and tariff/FX translation exposure.
